results.title: US poised to unveil new tariffs targeting S. Korea, 15 other trading partners
results.content: WASHINGTON — The Trump administration is poised to imminently release the findings of a probe aimed at countering alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major U.S. trading partners, three people with knowledge of the matter said on Tuesday, with new import duties on a wide range of goods expected. The results of the investigation under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 are expected as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday, these people said. The U.S. Trade Representative's office is expected to propose new duties that would stack on top of previous tariffs already imposed during Trump's second term. The duties would partly replace global import taxes struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February. results.title: US reaffirms alliance cooperation after Lee names new foreign, unification ministers, spy chief
results.content: WASHINGTON — The U.S. State Department on Tuesday stressed the importance of close cooperation with South Korea following President Lee Jae Myung's nomination of new officials to lead the country's foreign policy, intelligence and inter-Korean affairs. On Monday, Lee nominated Lim Woong-soon, currently the second deputy national security adviser, as foreign minister; former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil as director of the National Intelligence Service (NIS); and former lawmaker Hong Ihk-pyo as unification minister. "The United States values the importance of close cooperation in the U.S.-ROK Alliance," a State Department spokesman said in response to a query from Yonhap News Agency regarding the nominations of new Cabinet members and a new spy chief. results.title: Why do restaurants keep reusing leftover side dishes?
results.content: Click here for more articles by Kormedi.com. Reusing food left behind by customers poses serious hygiene risks and can spread diseases, including influenza and hepatitis. Food that other diners have stirred with their chopsticks may be contaminated with saliva. The risk is easy to understand if you think of the respiratory droplets that became a familiar concern during the COVID-19 pandemic. Restaurants caught doing this can face administrative sanctions, including business suspensions, as well as criminal penalties. Another restaurant has been caught reusing food left behind by customers. A district office in Seoul has begun administrative proceedings against a restaurant found to have violated the Food Sanitation Act.
